options.text: Fine ragi flour should pass through the sieve; larger grit should remain on the sieve.
Sieving is suitable here because the particles differ in size and the hole size sits between them.
With those hole sizes, fine ragi flour remains on the sieve and larger grit passes through.
The same sieve will remove dissolved mud colour from the muddy water.

stem:
Rohit needs to separate fine ragi flour from larger grit using a kitchen sieve whose holes are between the sizes of the flour and the grit. He also has a cup of muddy water on the side.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Sieving lets smaller particles through and keeps larger ones. Holes between flour and grit sizes make that separation work. Reversing which passes, or using a sieve for dissolved mud in water, is wrong.
